scenario: With a Float operand, `%` is the exact truncated remainder moved to the divisor's sign and `//` is derived from it, as CPython 3.12's float.__mod__ / __floordiv__ ([LEXP.7.6], [LEXP.7.5]). One rule per vector, each firing iff the result equals CPython's, every expected value printed under python:3.12 and never derived from a runtime; the large pairs come from a seeded search (seed 1602), |a/b| > 2^53. Operands are slots, so nothing folds at compile time. PATH PINNED: the Float arm of DS_RETE_BINOP_IDIV / DS_RETE_BINOP_MOD in runtime/src/libds/rete/eval.c (float_divmod over exact_fmod), and ds.eval's arith(op_floordiv) / arith(op_rem) (lexp_7_5_float_floordiv / lexp_7_6_float_mod over exact_fmod). WHAT EACH VECTOR PINS against a runtime using the formula a - b*floor(a/b), floor(a/b): the two large `%` vectors (it answers 0.0); the rest it gets right, and they pin the composition's ordinary cases. A runtime with no Float arm gives a type error on every vector. Pin: one fact, all eleven rules fire, in source order.
